strengths: Well-motivated approach with compelling examples (Spawrious) showing data-level bias analysis is insufficient
Novel perspective analyzing weight drift rather than data analysis alone for bias identification
Broad empirical evaluation across vision and text modalities (4 datasets)
Consistent empirical improvements in worst-group accuracy over baselines (Table 1)
Clear presentation with good visual illustrations (Figure 1) of the methodology
Includes ablation studies showing importance of design choices (Table 2)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: method combines existing techniques (linear probing, embedding arithmetic) without deep theoretical insights; Eq. 2 bound is basic triangle inequality
Indirect evaluation: primary metric (zero-shot prompting) indirectly measures bias quality; missing direct validation that identified concepts are actually spurious features the model uses
No human validation: Table 3 shows identified biases lack human evaluation of correctness; qualitative inspection reveals questionable identifications (e.g., 'beautiful' for blonde hair)
Incomplete baseline comparisons: CivilComments lacks comparisons with other methods; poorest results there (53.7% worst, 69.0% avg)
Critical bottleneck via image captioning: method quality limited by caption model; no mitigation strategy proposed despite acknowledged limitation
Ad-hoc concept extraction/filtering: YAKE and WordNet-based filtering are heuristic-driven with no ablation; requires task-specific preprocessing
No principled hyperparameter selection: Table 2 shows top-q matters significantly but no principled strategy offered (why 15 vs 30?)

Weak theoretical justification: Eq. 3 ranking design (minimum vs other class similarities) lacks principled justification; assumption that high-similarity concepts drive predictions not rigorously validated
Contradictory results: average accuracy often decreases substantially when worst-group improves (Table 1: Waterbirds 90.7→84.7), suggesting identified concepts may include legitimate features
Artificial evaluation setup: zero-shot prompting requires manual prompt engineering; results depend on prompt quality; doesn't directly measure model's use of concepts
Limited scope: only evaluated on well-studied benchmarks with known biases; no evaluation on real-world data with unknown ground-truth biases
Missing critical analyses: no feature attribution to validate concept importance, no human evaluation, no robustness analysis across FM architectures
Reproducibility concerns: many hyperparameters with limited justification; code availability not mentioned; caption/filtering complexity adds barriers
Overclaimed contributions: 'first weight-space approach' needs careful qualification; improvements described as 'significant' but often modest

strengths: Intuitive approach to bias detection via weight trajectory analysis in embedding space, offering a novel angle compared to data-analysis-only methods
Multi-modal evaluation across image (Waterbirds, CelebA, Nico++) and text (CivilComments) datasets demonstrating reasonable generality
Consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy across datasets (e.g., 35.2→55.3 on Waterbirds)
Well-motivated ranking score (Eq. 3) based on differential cosine similarity across class weights
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core method is straightforward application of cosine similarity ranking on normalized linear probe weights; Equation 2 provides only loose geometric bounds without deep insight

Evaluation lacks rigor: (1) Relies solely on artificial zero-shot prompting task rather than direct bias discovery quality metrics; (2) No human validation of discovered biases; (3) Biases discovered and evaluated on same data (potential overfitting); (4) Cherry-picks best templates without held-out validation; (5) No statistical significance testing
Critical limitations inadequately addressed: Captioning model (GIT-Large) is fundamental bottleneck for image tasks but no empirical analysis of bias discovery loss due to caption failures
Vague and underspecified method: Step 5 (filtering) poorly described; unclear justification for keyword extraction choices (YAKE, n-gram sizes 3 and 5, top-256/top-15 thresholds)
No validation of core assumption: Paper assumes weights drift toward spurious features but never empirically demonstrates this; weights could converge to class-relevant semantics instead
Incomplete and inconsistent baseline comparisons: CivilComments only compares to FM zero-shot baseline, not other debiasing methods; many dataset-baseline pairs marked as missing ('-')

Mixed empirical results: Improvements in worst-group accuracy come with notable trade-offs in average accuracy (e.g., 90.7→84.7 on Waterbirds); modest improvements on some datasets (2.8 pp on CelebA worst-case)
Unclear differentiation from concurrent work (Lg [37]): Both use embedding-space arithmetic; claimed difference ('weights drift' vs 'class-specificity score') is not well justified
Limited scope and scalability: Only tested on 2-4 class problems; single foundational model family (CLIP/mGTE); generalization to many-class scenarios or other vision-language models unexplored

Weak theoretical justification: Equation 2 shows expected behavior from initialization rather than evidence for bias discovery; no formal analysis of why weight analysis should outperform data analysis

strengths: Novel weight-space perspective on bias detection that diverges from data-centric approaches, providing a genuinely new angle on an important problem
Sound mathematical framework with ranked scoring system grounded in embedding-space geometry; principle clearly articulated through Equation 3 and supporting inequality
Comprehensive experimental validation across four diverse datasets (Waterbirds, CelebA, Nico++, CivilComments) spanning image and text modalities with consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy
Well-motivated zero-shot prompting evaluation strategy that provides practical validation of bias discovery quality by testing downstream impact
Clear methodology with detailed implementation specifications supporting reproducibility; method is straightforward to implement and adapt
Effective positioning relative to existing work (B2T, SpLiCE, Lg) with explicit comparison in Table 4 highlighting fundamental differences in approach
weaknesses: Critical bottleneck created by dependence on external captioning models (GIT-Large); acknowledged limitation that captioners don't extract all image details directly constrains bias discovery; no robustness analysis across alternative captioning models

Weak theoretical justification for core claim that weights drift specifically *towards biases* rather than other spurious features; the connection between drift and bias is intuitive but not rigorously established; inequality in Eq. 2 is loose and doesn't guarantee discovered concepts are actually biases

Evaluation methodology is indirect; zero-shot prompting improvements test generalization rather than directly validating bias identification; lacks quantitative evaluation of bias quality (no inter-rater agreement studies for Table 3 labels)

Ad-hoc filtering procedure in Step 5 relies on WordNet hierarchies with acknowledged limitations; filtering logic appears dataset-specific; no ablation on filtering procedure; residual class-related concepts remain (e.g., 'body of water' in Table 3 blue entries)

Critical design choices lack principled selection strategy: top-q sensitivity shown in Table 2 but authors explicitly state 'we leave finding a good cut-off strategy for future work'; concept extraction uses arbitrary parameters (256 n-grams, n ∈ {3,5}) without sensitivity analysis

Incomplete baseline comparisons with many entries marked '-' in Table 1 preventing comprehensive evaluation; some improvements modest (CelebA average 88.4 vs. 90.2 for competing methods); worst-group accuracy sometimes lower than alternatives
Statistical rigor concerns: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-run validation; results potentially sensitive to random initialization; no significance testing reported

Ethical concerns inadequately addressed: CivilComments biases include religious/ethnic terms (Table 6) which could perpetuate problematic associations if not carefully interpreted; limited discussion of responsible use and potential misapplication

strengths: Novel weight-space perspective: Analyzing model weights rather than predictions or data is conceptually fresh and overcomes the limitation that error-based approaches cannot detect spurious correlations absent from validation sets.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets (Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, ImageNet), multiple evaluation paradigms (synthetic image generation, fully spurious setup, zero-shot prompting), extensive ablations, and testing on 30+ ImageNet architectures.

Practical impact: Discovery of previously unknown spurious correlations in production-scale ImageNet classifiers (e.g., firefighters→Fire Truck) that fool multiple state-of-the-art models demonstrates real utility.

Consistent empirical improvements: Superior zero-shot performance over baselines (Table 5) and performance in extreme scenarios (100% spurious correlations) where prior methods like GroupDRO fail (Table 3).
Technical soundness: Algorithm is clearly presented, experimental setup is detailed, and results are reproducible with promised code release.
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification: The paper assumes weight drift encodes spurious correlations but provides limited rigorous justification for why this should be true. The ranking score (Eq. 2) and dynamic thresholding heuristic (Eq. 3) appear somewhat arbitrary without principled motivation.

Limited ImageNet validation: Only 3 out of many discovered spurious correlations are fully validated through synthetic images due to manual verification overhead. Remaining ImageNet findings (Appendix C) have lower credibility. Synthetic validation is indirect and may conflate classifier and generative model biases.

Critical pipeline dependency: Method depends on multi-stage concept extraction (GIT-Large captioning → YAKE extraction → LLM/WordNet filtering) with no sensitivity analysis or ablation on individual components. Quality and robustness of this pipeline is not thoroughly evaluated.

Inconsistent/unclear results: CelebA 'blonde hair' task yields no spurious correlations while baselines do—no explanation provided. Some findings in Table 4 marked as 'off-topic' using subjective criteria. Some zero-shot improvements are modest.

Modest technical novelty: Core components are standard (linear layers, dot products, smoothing). Novelty is in application rather than algorithmic contribution. Regularization approach is straightforward.

Limited generalization: Method restricted to linear probing on frozen foundation models. Applicability to end-to-end fine-tuning, other architectures, and non-CLIP models unclear. Fully spurious setup (100% correlation) is artificial and may not reflect realistic scenarios.

Fairness treatment is superficial: Paper tests on CivilComments then disclaims fairness implications. The distinction between spurious correlations and bias is left unexplored despite using bias-related datasets.

strengths: Novel perspective analyzing weight trajectories rather than predictions/errors for spurious correlation detection
Demonstrates multi-modal applicability across vision and text datasets (Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, ImageNet)
Addresses limitation of prior methods by identifying SCs without requiring validation set counterexamples
Comprehensive evaluation using multiple approaches: synthetic image generation, zero-shot prompting, regularization-based training
Clear algorithmic specification and promise to release code
weaknesses: Overclaimed novelty: Despite framing as transcending 'data and error analysis,' the method fundamentally depends on concept extraction pipelines (GIT captioning, YAKE), external filtering models (Llama-3.1, WordNet), and embedding spaces—all forms of data analysis

Acknowledged validation limitations severely undermine ImageNet claims: Authors state 'we were forced to restrict ourselves to presenting only a few of our findings' due to required manual verification of synthetic images, contradicting claims of automated large-scale SC discovery

Key design choices lack justification and ablation: (1) Dynamic thresholding heuristic (Eq. 3) appears arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameter r; (2) Concept extraction via GIT+YAKE chosen without ablation; (3) Filtering conflates relevance with causality; (4) Scoring function (Eq. 2) lacks theoretical grounding

Weak theoretical connection between methodology and claims: No formal justification for why weight drift reveals spurious vs. merely predictive features; circular reasoning risk for ImageNet evaluation (using CLIP to validate CLIP-discovered SCs)

ImageNet spurious correlations lack rigorous validation: No ground truth exists; many claimed SCs questionable (e.g., 'firemen' for Fire Truck seems like genuine visual feature); manual verification bottleneck acknowledged by authors; synthetic images don't rigorously establish causality

Limited quantitative evaluation of SC quality: Table 4 purely qualitative; Table 5 shows modest/mixed improvements (50.3 vs 46.1 for Waterbirds; underperforms LG on CelebA); Table 3 shows random class-neutral concepts also significantly help (46.6→50.4), questioning whether correct SCs were identified
Insufficient baseline comparisons: Mostly qualitative; missing recent spurious correlation methods; no statistical significance testing; inconsistent standard deviation reporting
Heavy unvalidated dependencies: Results depend on external models (GIT, YAKE, Llama-3.1, WordNet, CLIP/mGTE) with no sensitivity analysis; computational cost not analyzed
Missing critical ablations: No ablation on concept extraction components, filtering strategies, or impact of individual pipeline choices on final results

Problematic fairness treatment: Benchmarks CivilComments while disclaiming fairness intent; discovered racial/religious concepts lack adequate discussion of potential harms; insufficient boundary between bias detection and fairness

strengths: Novel weight-space approach to spurious correlation detection, offering a fresh perspective distinct from data/error analysis methods
Comprehensive multi-dataset evaluation (Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, ImageNet) with three complementary validation strategies (synthetic images, regularization, zero-shot prompting)
Compelling practical results including discovery of previously unknown spurious correlations in ImageNet and ability to fool state-of-the-art models with synthetic images
Demonstrates strong generality across modalities (vision and text) and multiple model architectures (50+ ImageNet models tested)
Clear presentation with excellent visualizations and detailed algorithmic description supporting reproducibility
Outperforms baselines (B2T, SpLiCE, LG) on standard benchmarks while achieving improvements even in extreme settings (100% spurious correlation)
Addresses practical problem with clear utility for practitioners working with foundation models
weaknesses: Core technical novelty is limited—individual components (linear probing, GIT captioning, YAKE extraction, embedding-space ranking) are standard; primary contribution is their combination
Dynamic thresholding formula (Eq. 3) appears ad-hoc and lacks principled justification; relies on heuristic that sorted scores deviate most from diagonal line

ImageNet validation strategy is problematic: only 3 examples manually verified despite claims of discovering spurious correlations; paper acknowledges 'complete investigation...ascribed to future work'; synthetic image artifacts could confound results
Heavy dependencies on auxiliary systems (GIT, YAKE, Llama-3.1, WordNet) with error propagation but no sensitivity analysis; inconsistent filtering (WordNet-only for ImageNet)
Lacks theoretical justification for why weights should drift toward spurious correlations or when method will fail; assumes linear layer weights encode all SCs without formal support
Fairness concerns inadequately addressed—includes CivilComments experiments but dismisses fairness considerations with disclaimer that feels defensive rather than principled
Limited error analysis: no discussion of failure modes, edge cases, or false positives; CelebA-blonde hair finding no SCs unexplained
No computational cost analysis despite expensive validation (1000 synthetic images × many concepts); scalability unclear
Missing ablation studies on critical components: sensitivity to caption models, keyword extractors, LLM prompts; no comparison of alternative thresholding schemes
Validation on standard benchmarks shows meaningful but not dramatic improvements (Table 3: 57.9% vs 50.4%); improvements on ImageNet not quantitatively validated at scale
